newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Lutherans approve blessing for gay partners.
newsitem.headline: German Lutherans approve blessing for gay partners.

text.p: A Protestant church council in northern Germany has decided to give homosexual couples the right to a church blessing if their partnership resembles a marriage, a German newspaper reported on Sunday.
Welt am Sonntag said a majority of the Lutheran church synod based in the town of Rendsburg also agreed to recognise any relationships that were similar to marriage in a landmark vote late on Friday.
But it was not clear whether the practice would go ahead because the synod's decision could still be vetoed by the church's bishops who had a month to decide on their position.
The Lutheran church was not immediately available for comment. The Protestant Church in Germany is an alliance of 24 largely independent Lutheran, Reformed and Untied churches.
There are about 30 million Protestants and 28 million Catholics in Germany.
